name: Objectivity/DB
tagline: Distributed, federated object database once used at petabyte scale in physics; vendor has ceased trading.
description: Objectivity/DB was a commercial object database with a distributed, federated architecture: many database files across many hosts presented as a single logical store, accessed through C++, Java, C# and Python APIs that followed the ODMG standard. It was famous for scientific and defence workloads, including SLAC's BaBar experiment, which held over a petabyte of objects, and it later spawned the ThingSpan and InfiniteGraph graph products. Objectivity, Inc. reportedly ceased operations in late 2023, and its website no longer serves product information. Treat it as discontinued.
statusNote: Objectivity, Inc. reportedly ceased operations in late 2023; objectivity.com no longer serves product pages and no releases or support are available.

scale.notes: Federated databases reached over a petabyte in the BaBar physics experiment.

strengths: Federated architecture spanning many hosts as one logical database
Proven at petabyte scale in high-energy physics
weaknesses: Vendor has ceased trading; no support or updates
useCases: Planning migrations off remaining Objectivity/DB installations
